summary: Dixit is a party game of visual storytelling where the storyteller gives an evocative clue for one of their surreal, dreamlike cards, and everyone else tries to submit a card from their own hand that could also match. It's beloved for sparking creativity and gentle social deduction with almost no rules overhead.
praised: Very easy to teach, works for all ages and non-gamers
criticised: Can feel repetitive over many plays
Storyteller can be too obvious or too obscure, unbalancing scoring
Groups that don't 'click' creatively can find it flat

interaction.kind: crafting a clue aimed at your fellow guessers while voting on everyone else's submitted cards
interaction.detail: The storyteller's clue must be judged against decoys other players contribute, and everyone's guess directly determines another player's score, so each round is a shared judgment exercise rather than parallel play. There's no private board or resource track; the entire game state is the shared table of cards and votes, though there is no blocking or denial of resources.
interaction.said: unknown — falls back on the game's targeted-clue and voting mechanics

scoring.how_you_win: As storyteller you want some but not all players to guess your card, and as a guesser you want to identify the storyteller's card while fooling others with your own; first to 30 points wins.
scoring.score_note: target is 30, or 40 with 6 players; round finishes so it can exceed target
